author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US is denying Iran’s claim that it destroyed a military early warning radar system in Bahrain.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says the strike was in retaliation for an attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, near the Strait of Hormuz. It has warned the US to stop what it calls aerial aggression and the smuggling of oil through the waterway.

The IRGC has also released footage of what it says is a tanker that exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine.

Al Jazeera’s Mohamed Vall says Iran has not confirmed the Bahrain strike. Iran appears confident they can retaliate against any new US attack, after several US attacks on Qeshm island in recent weeks drew no clear Iranian response.

There are no new announcements on negotiations. Iran says the ball is in the US court after presenting seven points, and that without a favourable response there will be no resumption of talks. It also says the Strait of Hormuz will remain under Iranian control.

Al
title: US denies Iran’s claim it destroyed early warning radar in Bahrain

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Pope Leo XIV has arrived in Peru, where he spent decades before becoming head of the Roman Catholic Church, for an emotional homecoming.

In Chiclayo, a city dear to the pontiff, he celebrated Mass on Friday. As a young missionary, Father Robert Prevost spent nearly two decades in Peru, including eight years as bishop of Chiclayo, where he ordained priests and helped communities recover from disasters.

Tens of thousands of Peruvians walked through dust and under a scorching sun across the Pimentel desert plain to pray with him. Thanking the crowd for their support and concern for his health, the Pope said: “What a joy to return to Chiclayo.”

Born in Chicago, Pope Leo says Chiclayo is his hometown. Residents say they feel privileged that a Peruvian Pope is from Chiclayo.

On the last leg of his Peru tour, he has called on political leaders to protect vulnerable Peruvians, asked the clergy to end sexual abuse and told young people to follow their dreams.

Al Jazeera’s Mariana Sanchez
title: Pope Leo returns to Chiclayo, Peru, in emotional homecoming

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Men, women and children have barely survived one of the world’s deadliest migration crossings after an Atlantic storm. Their boat was sinking when the Spanish Coast Guard found them, after at least six days at sea.

Boats are towed day and night to La Restinga port on El Hierro, the smallest and most westerly of the Canary Islands. Boats usually leave Senegal and sail far out into the Atlantic to avoid patrols further up the African coast. 

More than 7,500 migrants have landed on El Hierro in two weeks, before being sent to neighbouring islands or the mainland. Regional authorities say arrivals are unsustainable.

They land as a general election campaign starts. The government is regularising the status of hundreds of thousands of migrants, saying Spain needs immigration. Opposition parties say that creates a pull factor and strains schools and hospitals.

Overall, migrant arrivals are down 61% so far this year, but crossings usually pick up in autumn when sea conditions are more fav
title: Migrants rescued in Atlantic storm reach Spain’s El Hierro as election campaign begins

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The EU summit was meant to focus on AI, but leaders spent much of their time on who will represent them at the next round of talks to end the war in Ukraine.

They have agreed to what they call the E5 format: Italy, France, Poland, the UK and Germany, plus the European Commission and the European Council. The president of the European Council says Europe must speak with “one clear and united voice” in discussions shaping Ukraine’s future and the continent’s security.

EU top diplomat Kaja Kallas says Europe would walk into Russia’s traps if it diverted attention from the lack of a ceasefire and listened to its claims on security architecture.

There is also concern about what might happen if US President Donald Trump meets Russian President Vladimir Putin in China next week. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has sent Trump a message: no surprises.

Al Jazeera’s Milena Veselinovic reports from Dublin.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the US ground stop began at 3:36pm, when radar and communications at air traffic control centres and TRACONs became unstable. He says over 3,500 aircraft were in the air, with fewer than 400 left when he last checked, and that medevac and critical medicine flights were still allowed.

At a White House news conference, Duffy says the cause was an incredibly old system: analogue telecom switches and routers were overloaded and gave inconsistent data. He says new IP switches already installed did not fail. He says the airspace reopened at 8:15pm Eastern, but flights will resume slowly, depending on crews.

Duffy calls it an emergency and wants Congress to provide $50 billion, up from the $30 billion Trump requested, for a new system, saying $12.5 billion was included in the “One Big Beautiful Bill” as a down payment.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says the public was never in danger, the stop was out of an abundance of caution, and
title: US ground stop: US flights resume slowly as Duffy blames overloaded legacy air traffic systems

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Microsoft global outage has been impacting businesses and services in the UK.

In the National Health Service, doctors have reported difficulty accessing appointments for their patients, and pharmacies have reported delays in accessing prescriptions. Some police forces have been redirecting people away from their online reporting systems.

Government agencies and businesses that rely on Microsoft products such as Outlook and Teams are most affected, as are the millions of people who use them.

Microsoft says it has found no evidence of cyberattacks, but the outage put heavy pressure on its remaining working servers, making it harder to resolve. When one technology company has an issue, the problem goes around the world.

Al Jazeera’s Sonia Gallego reports from London.
